trust_decision.summary: UsersController::otp() accepts a paper (HOTP) token by verifying it against the hotp_counter cached in the session at password time instead of the stored counter, with no atomic burn, so a used token is accepted again (other session / concurrent request / same session after login).

landing_point.why: The summary names HOTP replay and the session-cached counter; the only HOTP verify call sits in otp().

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /users/otp, TOTP branch: fix adds Session->delete('otp_user') (fix.diff:21)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the email OTP race: 'the advisory is about paper HOTP tokens and the session-cached counter; email OTP is a separate factor that already deletes its code after use (app/Controller/UsersController.php:2207-2208)'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: TOTP login in the same action must keep working with no lock/counter, and HOTP must still accept the next unused paper code (the form shows the expected counter number, and hotp() lists codes from the stored counter); re-enrolment resets the counter to 0. Removing HOTP, adding a window, or locking/rejecting TOTP would break legitimate logins.

O6_input_shapes: single string OTP field User.otp, trimmed (fix.diff:28)

O7_producer.where: Session 'otp_user' written at app/Controller/UsersController.php:1414 (form login) and app/Controller/AppController.php:1737 (auth-plugin login), read at app/Controller/UsersController.php:2010

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Email OTP check is get-compare-then-del on Redis without a lock, so concurrent submissions can both pass before the code is burned (same single-use property, same Auth->login sink).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different second factor than the paper-token report; the code is already deleted after use, so it looks single-use.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 180 lines below the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A plugin-auth OTP shortcut (e.g. header-based re-auth on every request) that verifies HOTP inline against the cached $user['hotp_counter'] instead of redirecting to /users/otp.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This helper already handles the OTP state for plugin logins in another file; a maintainer avoiding the redirect loop described at lines 1749-1752 could plausibly verify in place.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The login step loads hotp_counter into the session-cached user, a data producer the otp() check trusts; a sibling in which a REST/JSON login returns or caches the counter would carry the same stale state.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: login() already selects User.hotp_counter explicitly at line 1398 just to carry it into the session.

O9_family: authentication: one-time second-factor token replay via stale cached state and non-atomic check-then-burn (CWE-287/CWE-362)

O10_build.project_tests: No unit tests for the OTP/login area found under app/Test (grep for otp matches only unrelated test names).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Re-read hotp_counter from the DB before verify (or bump the session copy) without an atomic lock/conditional update, leaving the concurrent-request race open and the email OTP get/del race untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: TOTP codes at app/Controller/UsersController.php:2023 can be reused within their validity window (no last-used timestep is stored); a separate property the fix did not address.
totp_delete clears totp but leaves hotp_counter (app/Controller/UsersController.php:2164); re-enrolment resets it at line 2116, so no impact seen.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check run).
present_in_latest unknown: no latest release given.
Whether the Overmind theme has its own otp view/endpoint that posts elsewhere was not checked; the grep found no second HOTP verify call in app/.
Pattern B is weak: the only uncovered route is the email OTP race, which a report about paper tokens may not obviously cover; the main how-type room is the session-cache producer (O7).
